heuristics.rule: If you are on PGWP, treat your job search as open-market; do not self-filter for LMIA-sponsoring employers
heuristics.condition: When a PM candidate is on PGWP and job searching in Canada...
heuristics.action: ...apply to any Canadian employer including startups and mid-size companies that do not sponsor LMIA, because PGWP is employer-unrestricted
heuristics.because: PGWP requires no LMIA and is open work authorization, so self-filtering to large LMIA sponsors artificially shrinks the candidate pool and wastes competitive advantage

heuristics.rule: Target 12 continuous months in a NOC TEER 1 PM role immediately after receiving PGWP
heuristics.condition: When a PM on PGWP wants to maximize PR optionality via Express Entry...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize securing a qualifying PM role quickly and tracking 12-month clock from day one of employment
heuristics.because: 12 months of TEER 1 experience unlocks Canadian Experience Class eligibility, which is the most reliable PR pathway for international graduates without requiring LMIA or employer sponsorship

heuristics.rule: If you are a US-based PM at a company with Canadian offices, use ICT transfer rather than LMIA to enter Canada
heuristics.condition: When a US-based PM wants to relocate to Canada and their employer has Canadian operations...
heuristics.action: ...pursue Intra-Company Transfer (C-12 exemption) instead of triggering LMIA process
heuristics.because: ICT is LMIA-exempt and avoids 2–5 month LMIA wait, making employment start immediate and reducing employer friction

heuristics.rule: For Indian or Chinese nationals, plan a 3-year horizon to Canadian citizenship before the Canada → US TN pathway becomes viable
heuristics.condition: When an Indian or Chinese national is building a Canada → US career path and expecting to use TN visa...
heuristics.action: ...factor in Canadian citizenship timeline (3 years of PR) before the TN option unlocks, and evaluate H-1B or EB-1A alternatives in parallel
heuristics.because: TN visa is only available to Canadian and Mexican citizens, not PR holders of non-North American nationality, making the timeline significantly longer for this group

heuristics.rule: Use Canada as a base for early-career PM experience and immigration security; plan US transition for mid-career scope maximization
heuristics.condition: When an ambitious PM is deciding whether to build their career in Canada or US long-term...
heuristics.action: ...treat Canada as a 2–4 year strategic platform for securing immigration status and building foundational experience, then evaluate US transition for principal/director-level scope
heuristics.because: Canadian PM experience is respected but Canadian market size structurally limits product scope and total comp relative to US; early career benefits outweigh later-career ceiling

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether LMIA is required and which employers will realistically consider you, dramatically affecting the size of the job market you can access
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify exactly: PGWP (open), Canadian PR/citizen (open), employer-specific permit (restricted), expired/no authorization (LMIA or new permit required)

decision_factors.factor: Nationality relative to TN visa eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the Canada → US TN pathway is accessible and on what timeline, which changes the long-term strategic value of pursuing Canadian PR
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Canadian or Mexican citizen = TN available now; non-North American national = TN requires citizenship, adding 3+ years to the path

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Many Canadian startups and mid-size companies refuse to do LMIA due to cost and time, effectively excluding candidates who require it from a large portion of the market
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine employer category: large tech (Amazon CA, Microsoft CA, major banks) = will do LMIA; startups/mid-size = often will not; assess via job posting language or direct recruiter inquiry

decision_factors.factor: Career ambition horizon: scope vs. stability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canada offers immigration security and lifestyle advantages; US offers higher comp and larger product scope — the right choice depends on which dimension the candidate is optimizing for
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the candidate's priority is maximizing PM career portfolio and comp, or securing long-term residency and work-life balance; these favor different geographies at different career stages

decision_factors.factor: Whether an intra-company transfer pathway exists
decision_factors.why_it_matters: ICT is LMIA-exempt and fast; if a candidate's current employer has Canadian operations, this is significantly easier than any external hiring pathway
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether current employer (especially US-based tech) has a Canadian entity; if yes, ICT C-12 exemption is likely available

decision_factors.factor: Global Talent Stream eligibility for the specific PM role
decision_factors.why_it_matters: GTS reduces LMIA processing from 2–5 months to 2 weeks, making it viable where standard LMIA is not; eligibility depends on NOC code of the PM role
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify whether the PM role is classified under NOC 20012; if so, employer may qualify for GTS expedited processing

decision_factors.factor: Time already accrued in TEER 1 Canadian work experience
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 12 months of TEER 1 experience is the threshold for CEC eligibility; every month matters when calculating how close the candidate is to PR eligibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count continuous months in NOC TEER 0 or 1 role on valid Canadian work authorization; assess gap to 12-month threshold

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Building a PM career in Canada rather than pursuing US roles directly
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Canadian PM product scope is structurally smaller due to market size, meaning portfolio stories are calibrated to a fraction of the user base and revenue of US equivalents — this creates a credibility gap when later competing for senior US PM roles
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Ambitious PMs who spend 5+ years in Canada and then try to compete for staff/principal US PM roles against candidates with global-product experience

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a PM role at a Canadian bank's digital division for stability and LMIA sponsorship
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Heavily regulated financial services environment shapes PM skills toward compliance-constrained, risk-averse product development — these skills transfer less cleanly to consumer tech or high-growth startup PM roles
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PMs who want to eventually move into consumer tech or growth-stage startups after banking PM experience

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Pursuing Canadian PR via Express Entry CEC pathway
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: For Indian and Chinese nationals, Canadian PR alone does not unlock TN to the US — citizenship (3 additional years) is required, meaning the full Canada → US path is 5–6+ years, not 2–3
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Indian and Chinese nationals who assume Canadian PR gives equivalent US access as it does for other nationalities

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Targeting only large LMIA-sponsoring employers (Amazon CA, major banks) due to work authorization constraints
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Excludes the majority of Canadian tech PM roles at startups and high-growth mid-size companies where PM scope, culture, and equity upside may be more valuable career investments
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PM candidates on employer-specific permits who self-restrict to large sponsors without exploring PGWP or GTS alternatives first

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Staying in Canada for lifestyle and immigration security rather than relocating to US for PM career growth
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Total compensation delta of 1.5–2.5× USD persists over an entire career, compounding significantly in savings, equity value, and retirement assets — the lifestyle trade has a quantifiable long-term financial cost
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PMs in mid-career who frame the Canada vs. US decision as annual salary difference rather than compounded lifetime earnings gap

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming Canadian PR gives TN visa access to the US for non-North American nationals
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates conflate immigration status with citizenship; PR grants Canadian residency rights but TN specifically requires citizenship of Canada or Mexico under CUSMA
failure_patterns.consequence: Indian and Chinese nationals plan a 2–3 year Canada → US timeline that is actually 5–6+ years, causing career planning miscalculations and missed US opportunities
warning_signs: Candidate says 'once I get Canadian PR I can use TN to go to the US'
Candidate is Indian or Chinese national who has not verified TN citizenship requirement

failure_patterns.pattern: Self-filtering to LMIA-sponsoring employers while on PGWP
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates carry over the mental model from post-study visa anxiety and conflate PGWP (open work authorization) with employer-specific permit restrictions
failure_patterns.consequence: PM candidates on PGWP unnecessarily exclude startups and high-growth companies, reducing job options and potentially settling for lower-quality roles at large institutions
warning_signs: PGWP holder only applies to Fortune 500 or major bank PM roles
Candidate asks startups about LMIA sponsorship before receiving an offer

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating Canadian PM experience as equivalent to US FAANG PM experience when targeting senior US roles
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates underestimate how much product scope and user base scale affects perceived seniority in US PM hiring; Canadian market size creates structurally smaller impact metrics
failure_patterns.consequence: PMs face unexpected leveling-down when interviewing for US roles, or fail to land roles they expected to qualify for based on title and years of experience
warning_signs: PM's portfolio stories reference Canadian-market-only products with limited scale metrics
PM assumes Director title in Canada translates directly to Director-level consideration at US companies

failure_patterns.pattern: Waiting out LMIA processing without securing interim work authorization or income
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates and employers underestimate LMIA processing time (2–5 months) and do not plan for the gap, assuming it will resolve faster than it does
failure_patterns.consequence: PM candidate cannot start work for months after expected start date; candidate may lose offer to another candidate or face financial hardship during wait
warning_signs: Employer says 'we'll start the LMIA process after you sign the offer'
Candidate has no bridging work authorization and is relying solely on LMIA approval timeline

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your current work authorization status in Canada — PGWP, Canadian PR, employer-specific permit, or none?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether LMIA is required and which segment of the PM job market is accessible, which is the single most important structural constraint in Canadian PM job searching
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If PGWP: confirm expiry date and months remaining; calculate whether CEC 12-month threshold is achievable within PGWP validity
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no valid authorization: determine whether LMIA, GTS, ICT, or a new study/work permit is the most viable pathway before job searching

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your citizenship — Canadian, US/Mexican, or other nationality?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines TN visa eligibility and therefore the viability and timeline of the Canada → US career path, which changes the long-term strategic value of pursuing Canadian PR
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Canadian citizen: TN to US is immediately available; Canada → US path is 1–2 years, not 5+
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Indian, Chinese, or other non-North American national: map out citizenship timeline; evaluate H-1B lottery and EB-1A as parallel paths to US

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your current or most recent employer have a Canadian legal entity?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: If yes, Intra-Company Transfer (ICT C-12 exemption) may be available, which is LMIA-exempt and significantly faster than any external hiring pathway
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Determine whether the Canadian entity is large enough to support an ICT transfer and whether the PM role has a Canadian equivalent; engage HR on ICT process
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Rule out ICT; assess Global Talent Stream eligibility based on NOC code of target PM role as next best LMIA-expedited option

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you optimizing for maximum PM career scope and compensation, or for immigration security and lifestyle stability?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Reveals which geography and employer type the candidate should prioritize — these goals favor fundamentally different career paths in Canada vs. US
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If scope and comp: Canada is appropriate for early-career base and PR, but US transition should be planned for mid-career principal/director level
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If stability and lifestyle: Canadian PM market at major banks or established tech companies is well-suited; accept comp ceiling as part of the tradeoff explicitly

diagnostic_questions.question: How many months of continuous NOC TEER 1 Canadian work experience have you accrued?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines proximity to the 12-month CEC eligibility threshold for Express Entry PR, which is the most actionable immigration milestone for PM candidates on PGWP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If 12+ months: assess current Express Entry CRS score and determine whether CEC draw is feasible in current cycle
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If less than 12 months: calculate exact months remaining; ensure current role's NOC code qualifies and that employment is continuous

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you targeting Canadian-headquartered companies, Canadian offices of US companies, or both?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Canadian offices of US companies (Amazon CA, Google CA) often offer stronger comp and global product scope, but hire fewer PMs; Canadian HQ companies offer more seats but smaller product scope and lower comp
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If US company Canadian offices: prepare for fewer total roles, more competitive process, and potentially global product context in interviews
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Canadian HQ only: calibrate comp expectations to Canadian market rates and prepare for regulated-environment or domestic-market product cases

industry_realities.common_belief: Canadian PM compensation is roughly comparable to US PM compensation after adjusting for cost of living
industry_realities.actual_reality: Canadian PM total comp is 1.5–2.5× lower in USD terms than comparable US PM roles, and this gap is not fully offset by cost of living differences in Toronto or Vancouver, which have high housing costs
industry_realities.implication: PMs should model the lifetime earnings gap explicitly rather than assuming cost of living adjustment neutralizes it; the compounded financial difference over a 20-year career is substantial

industry_realities.common_belief: Getting Canadian PR means you can easily move to the US on a TN visa
industry_realities.actual_reality: TN visa requires Canadian or Mexican citizenship, not just PR; for non-North American nationals, the path to TN is PR (1–2 years) plus citizenship (3 more years), totaling 4–5 years minimum
industry_realities.implication: Non-North American nationals should not rely on TN as their Canada → US pathway without planning for the full citizenship timeline; H-1B or EB-1A may be more time-efficient alternatives

industry_realities.common_belief: LMIA is a standard process that most Canadian employers will do for a strong PM candidate
industry_realities.actual_reality: Many Canadian startups and mid-size companies explicitly refuse to do LMIA due to cost ($1,000+) and 2–5 month processing time; only large employers routinely sponsor LMIA
industry_realities.implication: PM candidates who require LMIA should proactively qualify employer willingness before investing time in interview processes, and should prioritize pursuing PGWP or PR to remove this constraint

industry_realities.common_belief: Canadian PM interviews are just easier versions of US PM interviews with the same structure
industry_realities.actual_reality: Canadian PM interviews are structurally different: more behavioral/culture emphasis, fewer rounds (3–4 vs. 5–7), less pressure on estimation questions, and no Leetcode-style technical screens
industry_realities.implication: Candidates over-preparing for FAANG-style loops may over-invest in estimation and technical prep at the expense of behavioral depth, which is actually the higher-weight component in Canadian processes

industry_realities.common_belief: A Senior PM or Director title earned in Canada transfers directly to equivalent US leveling
industry_realities.actual_reality: Canadian PM Directors often oversee smaller product scope than US equivalents due to market size; US hiring committees calibrate on scope, user base, and revenue impact, not title alone
industry_realities.implication: PMs transitioning from Canada to US should reframe portfolio stories around relative impact and complexity rather than assuming title parity, and should anticipate potential leveling-down discussions

industry_realities.common_belief: Global Talent Stream is only for engineering roles, not PM roles
industry_realities.actual_reality: PM roles classified under NOC 20012 (Computer and Information Systems Managers) may qualify for Global Talent Stream, reducing LMIA processing from 2–5 months to approximately 2 weeks
industry_realities.implication: Employers and candidates should verify NOC code before defaulting to standard LMIA timelines; GTS can make PM hiring viable at companies that would otherwise decline to sponsor

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Understanding work authorization constraints in job searching
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Focuses only on qualifications and interview prep; treats work authorization as HR's problem to solve after an offer is received
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Maps work authorization status to employer eligibility before applying; qualifies LMIA willingness early in recruiter conversations to avoid wasted cycles
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Discovering authorization mismatch late in the process wastes months and damages candidate reputation with hiring teams who have invested interview time

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Evaluates Canada vs. US based on immediate salary number or current visa situation; does not model long-term career trajectory implications
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Models the full career arc: Canada for immigration security and early experience, with explicit decision point for US transition at mid-career to maximize scope and comp compounding
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Short-term optimization (take the Canadian offer now) can create structural career ceilings that are costly to overcome after 5+ years

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Assessing PM role quality beyond title and comp
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Evaluates offers primarily on base salary and job title; assumes Canadian bank Senior PM is equivalent to US tech Senior PM for future optionality
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Evaluates offers on product scope, user base scale, regulated vs. unregulated environment, and transferability of portfolio stories to future target roles
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A regulated bank PM role may offer LMIA sponsorship and stability but produce a portfolio that limits future mobility to consumer tech or global product companies

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Treats immigration status as a background constraint; assumes things will work out and focuses on the job search
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Maintains a live model of immigration milestones (months accrued toward CEC, Express Entry CRS score, PGWP expiry date) and proactively sequences job decisions to hit immigration thresholds
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A passive approach to immigration timing can result in authorization gaps that force accepting inferior roles or exiting Canada entirely due to status expiry

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Framing the Canada → US career path
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Views Canada and US as either/or choices; does not understand the structural mechanisms (TN, ICT, H-1B) that enable transitions between markets
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Understands each pathway mechanism and its conditions; uses Canada strategically as a platform with a planned US on-ramp once immigration and experience milestones are met
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Without understanding the mechanisms, candidates either stay in Canada by default or attempt US moves without the right authorization structure, creating unnecessary risk
